newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha weak, firm spot buyers yet to emerge.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha weak, firm spot buyers yet to emerge.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha prices were easier on Monday, reflecting weaker crude prices in a quiet market lacking firm direction, traders said.
Open-spec naphtha second-half March was notionally assessed at $229.50/231.00 and first-half April at $228.50/230.50, down from late Friday levels of $230.00/232.00 and $229.00/231.00, respectively.

The one-month spread from first-half April was assessed at 2.50/3.00. On Friday, first-half March/first-half April switched hands at $3.00, traders said. In the wet market, spot demand for March is seen weak due to higher term supplies.
One South Korean end-user has started sounding the market for March cargoes, traders said. Japanese buyers are still sidelined, they said.

In the low sulphur waxy residue market (LSWR), Indonesia Pertamina has allocated 3.7 million barrels for February loading. Traders said the allocation was larger in volume because unsold January cargoes had been carried over.

Traders expect Japanese demand to be poor and sales to hinge on South Korean demand. They assessed premium levels for March cargoes at about 70/90 cents above the Pertamina formula on an FOB basis, against about $1.00 for February cargoes.
